description: Grade 5 example: name an interval under a key signature (F major, treble clef).

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 10 addendum)

item.prompt: The key signature of F major is shown. Name the interval between these two notes (number and quality).

music.textAlternative: Two notes in F major (one flat, B♭): F4 and B♮4. The natural sign overrides the key signature. Both notes are minims.

hints: Apply the key signature to both notes before you count.
Count the letter names for the number, then compare with the major scale on the lower note for the quality.

feedback.correct: Correct. F major has B♭, but the natural sign makes this note B♮. F to B♮ is an augmented 4th (three whole tones); F to B♭ would be a perfect 4th.

mistakes.accidental-not-applied: Look at the sign beside the note. F major has B♭, but the natural sign makes this note B♮. F to B♮ is an augmented 4th (three whole tones); F to B♭ would be a perfect 4th.
mistakes.counted-one-end-only: Count both notes: the lower note is 1, then every letter name up to and including the upper note.
mistakes.quality-from-wrong-key: Judge the quality against the major scale of the lower note, using the sharps or flats actually sounding.

feedback.fallback: The answer is a augmentediminished  4. F major has B♭, but the natural sign makes this note B♮. F to B♮ is an augmented 4th (three whole tones); F to B♭ would be a perfect 4th.
